critical_evidence.evidence: No trunk-floor, spot-weld or differential-mount photos, and no inspection. CARFAX 'no structural damage' covers reported events only, not fatigue cracking.

There are no entries on CARFAX and no invoices. Some components (pump, thermostat, expansion tank, hoses) may be original at 25 years despite the low mileage. That is no reported entry, not proof the work was never done.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: VIN, itemised price, CARFAX with clean brands, 2 personal owners, a consistent odometer trail and the manual confirmed. The maintenance half is empty: no service records, no cooling or fluid dates, no photos of the trunk floor, subframe, underside or tire codes.

condition.rationale: Photos show glossy paint, a straight body, an intact tan top and a clean beige interior with only light creasing on the driver bolster. Nothing mechanical is proven. Very low use since 2015 means storage-related age items (cooling plastics, tires, seals, fluids) are open questions.

price_value.rationale: At $15,868 all-in it sits essentially at the fair-value mid of $15,567. That is below several active low-mile asks of $20k–27k, but with no records the likely age-related catch-up is unaccounted for.

mission_fit.rationale: It meets the brief: factory manual, 3.0i, about 25.6k miles, well inside the budget band, easy to resell. A 25-year-old soft-top BMW needs a convincing catch-up before year-round rain duty, and the profile ranks the MX-5 RF level with or above it.

logistics.rationale: The car is about 2,342 mi away in Florida. A mobile PPI at a dealer lot is normally arrangeable but is not confirmed. A fly-and-drive home on a lightly used car needs the catch-up first. CA smog and registration are likely feasible for a 2001 OBD-II car but unverified.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits: factory manual, 3.0i, dark green over beige with a tan top, stock and unmodified look, low miles. It is a roadster rather than the coveted coupe, and the sport package is not established.

what_would_change_verdict: Up: invoices showing cooling-system, fluid and tire renewal by date, plus clean trunk-floor and subframe photos or a specialist PPI.
Up: dealer confirms a mobile PPI before the deposit and provides tire dates under about six years old.
Down: subframe or trunk-floor cracking, active coolant loss, or significant oil leaks found at PPI.
Down: an AutoCheck that conflicts with the CARFAX (accident, extra owner, odometer), or a refusal of an on-site inspection.
evidence.mission_note: A factory-manual 3.0i under 60k miles within the budget band fits the enthusiast-bridge brief. It needs a documented age-related catch-up to be a year-round rain-capable daily, and the profile ranks a comparable MX-5 RF level with or above it.
evidence.rationale: The attached CARFAX establishes identity and history well: 2 personal owners since 2002, clean title brands, no reported accident or structural event, and an odometer trail consistent with 25,570 mi. The manual gearbox is confirmed separately by Jason. Photos show a stock-looking dark green 3.0i roadster with beige leather and a tan top in good cosmetic order, with only light wear on the driver's seat. What is observed is very low use since 2015, about 3,100 mi in 8.7 years, and no service entries on the report despite the summary claiming one. That is no reported entry, not proof of neglect. Both model-critical items, rear subframe and trunk-floor condition and cooling-system history, are entirely undocumented, as are tire dates, top condition and fluid ages. At $15,868 with the dealer fee included, the price sits at the fair-value mid of $15,567. The open questions concern maintenance evidence and inspection access rather than identity.
evidence.next_action: Ask Honest Autos for tire DOT code photos, trunk-floor and underside photos, any service or reconditioning invoices, and written agreement to a mobile pre-purchase inspection on their lot before any deposit.
